caption: Khalil v. President
citation_line: Khalil v. Joyce, 777 F. Supp. 3d 369 (D.N.J. 2025), vacated sub nom. Khalil v. President United States of America, Nos. 25-2162 & 25-2357 (3d Cir. Jan. 15, 2026)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Farbiarz held that the District of New Jersey could hear Mahmoud Khalil’s habeas petition, concluding that a habeas court with jurisdiction does not lose it when the petitioner is moved out of the district, and that 8 U.S.C. § 1252(b)(9) did not strip the court of jurisdiction over the claims before it.
qualification_rationale: A decision of first impression in the circuit on where a habeas petition lies after rapid interstate transfers, and on the reach of the INA’s channelling provision over claims brought alongside removal.
appellate_posture_note: A divided precedential Third Circuit panel agreed that the New Jersey court had habeas jurisdiction as the district of confinement, but held that 8 U.S.C. § 1252(b)(9) stripped subject-matter jurisdiction over the removal-related claims. It vacated the challenged orders and remanded with instructions to dismiss.
decision_selection_note: ECF 214, the published jurisdictional opinion, one of two entries split from a single record on 15 September 2026. The preliminary injunction is ECF 272.
